The Fourier resolvent has squared modulus1/(xi^2+1/4). With the exact probability density, Q(g)=cN Cov(X,1/(X+1/4)) is strictly negative. Strictness uses actual nonzero continuous Fourier density, not a separate positivity premise.

The exact variance is cN Var(X)=4pi^2 Delta/L^2. The frozen Delta bound gives the stated 8192pi^2+512 remainder. The resolvent remainder uses the H3 moment globally, yielding64 times two 5443200pi^4 allowances. The limit constant -16d0=-350/(11pi^2) is correct.

The same-eta exponential bound follows from sqrt(L)<=sqrt(L-v)+sqrt(v). The minimum of L/2-eta sqrt(L) is -eta^2/2, which pays the lower endpoint. The displayed K_eta and C_err cover both squared norm expansions. L^4 exp(L-eta sqrt(L)) is o(L^2 exp L).

The actual finite ratios expansion has exactly one term per p<q. The diagonal vanishes by native norm balance; the ordered cross terms combine to k_L, with no missing factor2. This is A_L^*A_L, whereas Selberg A_L^2 uses product shifts and different support.
